subject: Vendor onboarding + PO policy for TC Cloud integration
messages:
From: Alex Martin <alex@tccloud.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-23T08:15:00-08:00
Subject: Quick question — PO requirement for initial integration

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — excited to get TC Cloud integrated with Redwood for the analytics export. Procurement here is a bit slow on our side, and I wanted to check Redwood's PO requirement for new vendors. Our typical process is to invoice Net 30, but we don't always issue a PO for first-month professional services for smaller integrations.

We have a tight timeline and aim to go-live for the integration on Feb 10. Can you confirm whether Redwood requires a purchase order before we can start work, or whether an initial invoice + signed SOW would be acceptable for a short-term exception?

Attached: tccloud_w9.pdf (company W-9)

Quick company details:
- TC Cloud Solutions (EIN: 12-3456789)
- Contact: Alex Martin, Head of Partnerships
- Billing email: billing@tccloud.com

Happy to hop on a 15-min call if that helps.

Best,
Alex
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martin <alex@tccloud.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-23T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick question — PO requirement for initial integration

Alex — thanks for the note and the W-9. Glad the demo was helpful.

Short answer: our baseline is that Finance issues/records a PO for any vendor spend above our low-dollar threshold, but there is an established one-time exception path for time-sensitive integrations. Laura / Finance — looping you in for approval and to confirm the exact conditions.

Proposed mutual action plan (if this helps speed approvals):
- TC Cloud to send signed SOW (we can accept DocuSign).
- TC Cloud to complete the vendor onboarding packet (I attached our vendor packet).
- Finance to confirm PO-exception (scope & dollar cap) and provide invoice instructions.
- If approved, TC Cloud invoices Net 30 and we tag the invoice as PO_EXCEPTION-20260123.

Laura — suggested cap to consider: initial integration professional services up to $25k without a PO; renewals or ongoing spend will need a PO. If you prefer a different number or conditions, please advise.

I attached our vendor packet for your convenience: tccloud_vendor_packet.pdf

Alex — if you can turn around the SOW and the completed packet by Monday, we can aim to get finance approval the same week.

Thanks — Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-24T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Quick question — PO requirement for initial integration

Neha / Rishi — thanks for the context. Our standard procurement policy requires a PO for vendor spend greater than $5,000. That policy exists for tracking and audit reasons.

For time-sensitive integrations, Procurement can approve a limited, documented exception under these conditions:
1) We receive a signed SOW or contract for the scope of work (DocuSign link or PDF).
2) Vendor completes and returns the vendor onboarding form (banking + tax info).
3) AP receives the invoice referencing the exception ID and is sent to ap@redwood.com.
4) The exception is limited to a one-time spend cap — we will approve up to $25,000 for the initial integration.
5) Approval window: 60 days from the date of this email.

If the above are satisfied, Procurement will authorize a PO_EXCEPTION code (PO_EXCEPTION-20260123) that AP uses when recording the invoice. Renewals or follow-on work must be covered by a standard PO.

I have signed the exception approval; attaching signed confirmation (po_exception_approval_signed.pdf). Please have TC Cloud return the completed onboarding form so we can record banking info and insurance.

For compliance: we also need proof of general liability insurance and the completed onboarding spreadsheet.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Finance Manager, Procurement | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com

Attachments: po_exception_approval_signed.pdf (signed exception), vendor_onboarding_form_template.xlsx
From: Alex Martin <alex@tccloud.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-25T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick question — PO requirement for initial integration

Thanks everyone — we appreciate the fast turnaround and the exception. Per Laura's list, we've signed the SOW and completed the onboarding form; attached is the signed SOW (tccloud_sow_signed.pdf). I'll follow up with the onboarding spreadsheet and insurance certificate to ap@redwood.com shortly.

We accept the $25k one-time cap and the 60-day window. We'll route the invoice to ap@redwood.com and include the PO_EXCEPTION-20260123 tag on the invoice number.

Next steps (as we see them):
- TC Cloud to submit onboarding packet + insurance to AP (by EOD 1/26)
- TC Cloud to send first invoice once work begins (include exception tag)
- Neha to confirm kickoff date after paperwork is in place

Appreciate the help — Alex
Alex Martin
Head of Partnerships | TC Cloud Solutions
alex@tccloud.com
